SERACH.description: Serach was a Jewish woman noted as the daughter of Asher and granddaughter of Jacob. Her unique longevity and lineage are recorded in the Torah in Bereshit (46:17) and Bamidbar (26:46). She was a wise figure, known for gently breaking the news to Jacob that Joseph was still alive. The bracelet is crafted with organic tones and timeless symbolic elements. Natural agate and jasper beads in cream, grey, ochre and earthy red enhanced with spacer beads, anchored by a Magen David and a Tree of Life.

ELISHEBA.description: Elisheba (Shemot 6:23) was a woman of noble lineage, the daughter of Aminadab, sister of Nahshon and wife of Aaron the High Priest. She was the mother of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. Nadab and Abihu died while offering "unauthorised fire" before God. The bracelet is designed with sophisticated, warm-toned contrast of alternating black faceted beads and translucent, amber-brown crystals, enhanced with spacer rings, Magen David, a brilliant solitaire crystal charm and a brand tag.

SHELOMITH.description: Shelomith bat Dibri was a Jewish woman from the tribe of Dan, married to an Egyptian. She was the only woman mentioned in the Book of Vayikra, when her son blasphemed the Divine Name and got stoned to death. (24:10-23) The bracelet features dark, faceted black beads that offer a rich, deep texture. They are separated by small, warm, gold-toned spacer beads and an ornate filigree bail. The piece is anchored by a Tree of Life pendant charm alongside a round engraved "Ein Sof" brand tag.

COZBI.description: Cozbi was a Midianite princess and the daughter of Zur. Her story is recorded in the Book of Bamidbar (25:1-18). During the encampment at Shittim, she and her Jewish lover Zimri, the son of Salu, were both slain by Pinchas. Apparently Pinchas's act halted the plague during the crisis at Shittim. The piece is made with bright blue beads and sparkling clear crystal beads set within crescent moon frames, Special accents include: a silver-toned Hamsa pendant and a dangling pearl charm.

DEBORAH PROPHETESS.description: Deborah was a revered prophetess, judge and poet who led the nation of Israel during a critical time of oppression. (Shoftim 4 and 5). Sitting beneath the palm tree she rendered judgement and that's why the bracelet is designed with energetic, sunny tones and meaningful symbolism. It is anchored by a classic Magen David charm alongside an engraved gold-toned medallion featuring the Libra constellation.

YEHUDITH.description: Yehudith was a heroic and pious Jewish widow associated with the era of the Maccabean struggle and Chanukah traditions. She saved Jewish people by entering the camp of the invading Assyrian general Holofernes, seducing him and then vanquishing him to deliver the city. The bracelet is made of white beads and rich blue marbled imperial jasper beads separated by small, crystal-embedded spacer rings. It is anchored by a Menorah charm, celebrating her deep connection to the themes of Chanukah.

SHULAMITE.description: The Shulamite is the central female figure and beloved in the poetic text of Shir ha-Shirim, traditionally attributed to King Solomon. Her name appear in Shir ha-Shirim 6:13. The bracelet is an elegant, refreshing piece featuring white and grey-veined  paired with bright turquoise-blue round beads anchored by a Magen David and complemented by dangling charms including a musical treble clef pendant and a round engraved "Ein Sof" brand tag.

HOGLAH.description: Hoglah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad, belonging to the tribe of Menasseh. (Bamidbar 26:33, 27:1-11, Yehoshua 17:3). Together with Mahla, Noa, Milcah and Tirza she courageosly approached Moses and demanded a land inheritance after their father died without sons. The bracelet is a serene, earthy piece with classic detailing. It features green jade-style stone beads and a Magen David charm, offering a calming, organic look.

MAHLAH.description: Mahlah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad, belonging to the tribe of Menasseh. (Bamidbar 26:33, 27:1-11, Yehoshua 17:3). Because their father died without sons, Mahlah and her sisters petitioned Moses to request a land inheritance among their father's relatives. They were successful. The Mahlah bracelet is a sleek, bold, modern piece designed with striking contrast and structured geometry. Black, cube-style beads offer an unusual, sophisticated look.

JOCHEBED.description: Jochebed was a courageous daughter of Levi who became the wife of Amram and the mother of Miriam, Aaron and Moses. (Book of Shemot 2:1-10, 6:20). The bracelet is a sleek and modern piece designed with clean, geometric lines and cool tones. It catches the light from multiple angles. It is anchored by a Magen David and an engraved "Ein Sof" brand tag.

TIRZA.description: Tirza was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad, belonging to the tribe of Menasseh. Alongside her sisters, she successfully petitioned Moses for a land inheritance, establishing a biblical precedent for women's property rights. (Bamidbar 26:33, 27:1-11, Yehoshua 17:3). The bracelet features a striking pattern of luminous white pearl beads separated by dark, geometric spacer beads. A Magen David and the number 613 (commandments) elegantly accent the piece.

JUDITH.description: Judith was one of the wives of Esau, (sometimes identified as the same woman as Oholibamah, sometimes as a separate wife). A daughter of Beeri the Hittite. She features in the Book of Bereshit (26:34). The bracelet is made of translucent aqua-teal glow-in-the-dark beads embedded with speckled, luminous particles that shine in low light. It is anchored with a Magen David charm.

RUTH.description: Ruth was a Moabite woman who married into a Jewish family and, following the death of her husband, made the profound commitment to stay with her mother-in-law Naomi, declaring "Your people will be my people"... (The Book of Ruth) The bracelet features luminous white pearls paired with deep blue and turquoise-shaded agate beads. It is accented with cluster of charms, including a miniature book pendant and a vibrant blue and teal enamel Hamsa.

TZIPORAH.description: Tziporah (whose name means "bird") was the daughter of Jethro, the priest of Midian, and became the wife of Moses and the mother of Gershom and Eliezer. Her story features in the Book of Shemot (2:16-22, 4:24-26) The bracelet is made with eclectic array of colorful, crackled quartz-style beads in shades of pink, yellow, blue, purple and earth tones. It is accented with a dangling Hamsa hand charm alongside a charming enamel bird pendant.

DINAH.description: Dinah was the daughter of Jacob and Leah, and her narrative is featured prominently in the Book of Bereshit (Chapter 34). Her story centers on her experiences in the land of Canaan and her encounter with Shechem. The Dinah bracelet is made of alternating deep magenta-pink beads and pink quartz stones separated by antique-gold spacer beads. The piece is accented with a cluster of dangling gold-toned charms, including a Hamsa hand, a Tree of Life pendant and an engraved Ein Sof brand tag.

NOA.description: Noa was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad, belonging to the tribe of Menasseh. She features in the Book of Bamidbar (26:33, 27:1-11) as she and her sisters approach Moses to request a land inheritance after their father died without sons. The bracelet features smooth, soothing pale blue-grey chalcedony beads alternated with small, clear crystal beads. It is anchored by a silver Magen David charm.

BILHAH.description: Bilhah was the handmaid of Rachel who became the wife of Jacob and mother to two of the tribes of Israel: Dan and Naphtali. She features in the Book of Bereshit (29:29, 30:3-8). The Bilhah bracelet is made of translucent ruby-red beads separated by silver-toned metal beads for a balanced contrast. It is accented with a dangling silver-toned Magen David charm alongside an engraved EinSof brand tag.

ZILPAH.description: Zilpah was the handmaid of Leah who became the wife of Jacob and mother to two of the tribes of Israel. (Gad and Asher) She features in the Book of Bereshit (29:24, 30:9-13) The Zilpah bracelet is a warm, elegant stretch piece designed with earthy tones and gold accents. It catches the light beautifully.

SHIPHRAH.description: Shiphrah was one of the courageous Hebrew midwives in the Book of Shemot (1:15-21). Alongside Puah, she defied Pharaoh's decree to kill newborn Jewish boys, choosing instead to fear God and preserve the lives of the children. The bracelet features a striking contrast of deep ruby-red beads alternated with clusters of sparkling faceted clear crystal beads. A silver-toned Magen David charm anchors the piece.

DELILAH.description: Delilah is a complex figure featuring in the Book of Shoftim, chapter 16. Delilah sought to discover the secret of Samson's strength, ultimately uncovering that his power lay in his nazirite vow and unbroken hair. The bracelet is a striking bold piece designed with dramatic contrast and deep mystery. Smooth, glossy, black beads, gold-toned spacer beads and a delicate gold-toned Magen David, alongside a translucent central accent bead.

PUAH.description: Puah was one of the heroic Hebrew midwives immortalised in the Book of Shemot (1:15-21). Puah and Shiphrah defied Pharaoh's orders and preserved the lives of Jewish children. Puah bracelet is designed to honour preservation of life. It is made of amethyst beads, soft grey-blue agate stones and natural earthy stones, separated by glittering spacer rings. Silver toned Magen David symbolizes heritage, identity and protection.

MACHALATH.description: Machalath was the daughter of Ishmael, the sister of Nebajoth and one of the wives of Esau. Esau was only one of her many husbands. She features in Bereshit 28:9. A striking strand of dark, bronze-speckled glow-in-the-dark beads alternated with sparkling clear faceted crystal spacers. The only "Jewish" feature of the bracelet is a centered silver Magen David charm.

OHOLIBAMAH.description: Oholibamah was a daughter of Anah (the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite) and one of the wives of Esau. She gave Esau three sons: Jeush, Jalam and Korah, whose clans became prominent in the land of Edom. Book of Bereshit 36:2, 14 and 18. A captivating strand of deep blue glow-in-the-dark beads embedded with luminous specks, accented by smooth silver beads and a centered silver Magen David.

RACHEL.description: Rachel was the younger daughter of Laban, the cousin and beloved wife of Jacob and the mother of Joseph and Benjamin. One of the principal Matriarchs of Judaism. She was a compassionate mother weeping for and comforting her children. She features in Bereshit 29 and 35. A rich strand of deep red translucent beads separated by finely textured antique-gold spacers and a prominent central bead cap. The bracelet is accented with a round branded Ein Sof tag and a rectangular Tree of Life charm.

BASEMATH.description: Basemath was a daughter of Ishmael and the sister of Nebajoth, she became one of the wives of Esau. She is mentioned in Bereshit 36:3. An ornate, elegant strand featuring alternating polished gold spheres and white marbled beads accented with multiple Magen David charms.

KETURAH.description: Keturah was the wife whom Abraham married after the death of Sarah. She bore him six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah. Their descendants settled in the East. She features in the Book of Bereshit 25:1-4 and Divrei Hayamim 1:32. A classic, lustrous strand of smooth white pearl beads accented with sparkling small blue crystal bicone spacers. A solid silver toned Magen David centered along the strand.

DEBORAH.description: Deborah was a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth. She was one of the female leaders of Israel. She can be found in the Book of Shoftim (4 and 5). A vibrant strand of marbled turquoise blue beads separated by golden spacer balls with a striking central Magen David charm encrusted with crystals and a charming light blue and white enamel bird pendant.

REBEKAH.description: Rebekah (Rivka) was the daughter of Bethuel, the granddaughter of Nahor and Reumah, the sister of Laban and the wife of Isaac. One of the Matriarchs of Judaism, known for her kindness and strength. Mother of Jacob and Esau. She features in Bereshit 24 and Bereshit 27. Golden amber colour crystal beads with small gold spacer balls accented with miniature Magen David and dual Tree of Life pendants.

REUMAH.description: Reumah was the concubine of Abraham's brother Nahor. She had four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah. She features in Bereshit 22:24. An elegant interplay of contrasting monochromatic beads, including textured white stones, smooth translucent rounds, polished dark spheres and sparkling crystals. The bracelet is dangled with a delicate Magen David charm.

LEAH.description: Leah was the elder daughter of Laban, the first wife of Jacob and one of the four biblical matriarchs of Israel. She features in the Book of Bereshit (29-30, 49:31). The bracelet is made with alternating cubic beads in rich shades of blue, yellow and black, accented with small metallic silver tone spacers, Magen David and a distinctive honey pot charm.

HAGAR.description: Hagar was an Egyptian woman who served as a handmaiden to Sarah. Hagar gave birth to Abraham's son Ishmael. She features in thee Book of Bereshit. Golden-brown crystal beads with charms.

ISCAH.description: Warm faceted amber toned crystals interspersed with golden spacer accents, evoking timeless elegance. Magen David motif in the centre of the piece adds to it deep cultural resonance. Iscah was recorded in the Book of Bereshit (11:29) as the daughter of Haran and sister of Milcah.

MILCAH.description: Milcah bracelet handcrafted with striking turquoise-veined blue beads separated by silver toned spacers is a graceful celebration of legacy. Milcah was the daughter of Haran, the niece of Abraham and the wife of Nahor. She was also the grandmother of Rebekah. She features in the Book of Bereshit in verses 11:29, 11:31 and 22:20-23.

SARAH.description: This bracelet radiates warmth, elegance and heritage through  luminous, pearl-like beads nested in circular rings decorated with three Magen David charms. Sarah was the first of the matriarchs, the wife of Abraham and the mother of Isaac. She appears throughout the Book of Bereshit. (From 11:29....23:2)

MIRIAM.description: Square bluish beads in oval stainless steel frames with Magen David and musical charm. It is a radiant expression of heritage, rhythm and grace. Miriam was a prophetess, the older sister of Moses and Aaron. After the splitting of the Red Sea she takes a timbrel in her hand and leads the women in dance. (Shemot 15:20-21)

EDITH.description: A stony colours bracelet with Magen David spacer. Edith or Ado was the wife of Lot. Her name is not mentioned in the Chumash but she appears in the Book of Bereshit within the narrative of Sodom's destruction. She looked back and became a pilar of salt.

NAAMAH.description: Blue and white bracelet with Magen David spacers. Naamah is mentioned in the Book of Bereshit (4:22) as the daughter of Lamech and Zilah.

CHAVA.description: Blue, white and black glass bracelet with Magen David spacer. Chava was the mother of all the humans, she is mentioned in the Book of Bereshit (3:20, 4:1, 4:2)

ZILLAH.description: Sparkly pink beads with Magen David charm. Zillah was one of the two wives of Lamech and the mother of Tubalcain and Naamah. She is mentioned in the fourth chapter of the Book of Bereshit.

ADAH.description: White crystals bracelet with Magen David spacer. Adah was one of the two wives of Lamech and the mother of Jabal and Jubal. Her name appears in the Book of Bereshit (4:19-23)
